descriptions.village: A cluster of homes, farms and workstations. Meet villagers, trade supplies and look for a place to rest.
descriptions.desert-pyramid: A sandstone landmark with a concealed treasure chamber. Explore carefully: the lower chamber is trapped.
descriptions.jungle-temple: A moss-covered temple hidden in dense jungle. Watch for tripwires and search its redstone passages.
descriptions.swamp-hut: A small wooden hut above the swamp. Witches make these secluded structures dangerous places to approach.
descriptions.igloo: A snow shelter in cold landscapes. Some hide a basement beneath the floor.
descriptions.ocean-ruin: Submerged ruins scattered across the seabed. Bring air and light before exploring their remains.
descriptions.shipwreck: The remains of a wooden ship, underwater or along the shore. Search the surviving hull and cabins.
descriptions.monument: A large prismarine fortress beneath the ocean, guarded by guardians. Prepare for a sustained underwater expedition.
descriptions.mansion: A sprawling woodland home occupied by illagers. Its many rooms reward careful exploration.
descriptions.outpost: A pillager watchtower with a hostile patrol presence. Approach with cover and a clear escape route.
descriptions.ruined-portal: A broken portal surrounded by scattered obsidian. Inspect the frame before attempting to rebuild it.
descriptions.ruined-portal-nether: A ruined portal in the Nether. Its damaged frame may help you plan a route between dimensions.
descriptions.ancient-city: A vast underground ruin in the deep dark. Move quietly around sculk sensors and shriekers.
descriptions.trail-ruins: Buried remnants of an old settlement. A brush lets you investigate suspicious gravel without breaking it.
descriptions.trial-chambers: An underground copper-and-tuff complex with combat trials. Explore its chambers prepared for repeated encounters.
descriptions.abandoned-camp: A deserted campsite in the Overworld. Search its chests and barrels for supplies and explorer maps.
descriptions.fortress: A network of dark bridges and corridors in the Nether. Look for blazes and watch the exposed walkways.
descriptions.bastion: A massive blackstone remnant occupied by piglins. Its broken halls and lava make navigation hazardous.
descriptions.end-city: Tall purpur towers on the outer End islands. Watch for shulkers and dangerous falls.
descriptions.stronghold: A buried stone-brick complex containing the portal route to the End. Search its corridors carefully.
descriptions.mineshaft: An abandoned underground network of timber supports, rails and minecart chests. Watch for cave spiders and sudden drops.
descriptions.buried-treasure: A hidden chest buried beneath coastal sand or gravel. The marker identifies its seed-based candidate location.

groupDescriptions.settlements: Homes, strongholds and watchtowers: places to meet inhabitants, trade or face hostile occupants.
groupDescriptions.exploration: Temples, buried ruins and underground challenges. Each landmark offers a different kind of expedition.
groupDescriptions.ocean: Shipwrecks, submerged ruins and guardian fortresses. Prepare for limited air and underwater travel.
groupDescriptions.portals: Damaged gateways between dimensions. Inspect their surroundings and plan your route.
groupDescriptions.nether: Fortified structures among lava and hostile terrain. Bring supplies and keep a safe return path.
groupDescriptions.end: Remote towers beyond the central island. Plan for long crossings, shulkers and falls.

highlights.ancient_debris: A rare Nether ore. Smelt it into netherite scrap to begin making netherite equipment.
highlights.netherite_scrap: Smelt ancient debris to get scrap. Four scraps and four gold ingots make one netherite ingot.
highlights.netherite_ingot: Combine four netherite scraps with four gold ingots. Use the ingot at a smithing table to upgrade diamond gear.
highlights.diamond: Mine diamond ore or find diamonds in loot. Diamonds make strong equipment and an enchanting table.
highlights.emerald: The main currency for villager trading. Get emeralds from trades, emerald ore or loot.
highlights.iron_ingot: Smelt raw iron for this versatile material used in tools, armor and utility blocks.
highlights.gold_ingot: Smelt raw gold or find ingots in loot. Gold makes equipment, powered rails, golden food and netherite.
highlights.redstone: Redstone dust carries signals between components and is an ingredient in many circuit parts.
highlights.blaze_rod: Blazes in Nether fortresses drop rods. Turn them into blaze powder or craft a brewing stand.
highlights.ender_pearl: Throw an ender pearl to teleport, or use it to craft an Eye of Ender for finding a stronghold.
highlights.elytra: Wings found in End ships that let you glide. Firework rockets can extend your flight.
highlights.totem_of_undying: Hold a totem in either hand to survive otherwise fatal damage. Evokers drop them.
highlights.shulker_shell: A shulker drop. Combine two shells with a chest to craft a portable shulker box.
highlights.nether_star: Defeat the Wither to obtain this rare ingredient for a beacon.
highlights.cushion: Place this cushion on a flat surface to sit on it. Craft it from three matching wool slabs; it breaks if its support is removed.
highlights.woolStairs: A colored wool stair for building and decoration. Craft it from matching wool blocks.
highlights.woolSlab: A colored wool slab for building and decoration. It can also be crafted into a matching cushion.
highlights.concreteStairs: A colored concrete stair for building and decoration. Craft it from matching concrete blocks or use a stonecutter.
highlights.concreteSlab: A colored concrete slab for building and decoration. Craft it from matching concrete blocks or use a stonecutter.
highlights.poplarWood: Poplar wood comes from the Dappled Forest and can be crafted into a full set of wooden building blocks and items.
highlights.poplarSapling: Poplar saplings grow into red, orange or yellow poplar trees. They can also be offered by wandering traders.
highlights.strawBed: Sleep through the night without setting your respawn point. A straw bed is used once and is destroyed if used in the Nether or End.
highlights.redShrub: A plant found in the Dappled Forest. Bone meal can spread it to a nearby space, and it can be composted.
highlights.shelfMushroom: Grows on poplar trees in the Dappled Forest. Bone meal grows the small form; the large form drops two mushrooms. It can be used in stew.

groupIntro.fundamentals: These parts create, carry, change or measure a redstone signal.
groupIntro.inputs: Inputs turn player actions or world events into a redstone signal.
groupIntro.outputs: Outputs react when a redstone signal reaches them.
groupIntro.automation: These blocks move or craft items and can be controlled by redstone.

redstoneGuide.lineIntro: Switch the lever and change the line length. Add a repeater after 15 dust segments to see when the lamp lights.
redstoneGuide.rangeNote: The first dust segment has strength 15. Each additional segment loses one; add a repeater before it reaches zero.

redstone.behavior: Place redstone dust to carry a signal between components. A full-strength signal reaches up to 15 dust segments.
redstone.example: Connect a lever to a lamp with dust. Extend the line and add a repeater when the lamp stops lighting.

redstone_block.behavior: A redstone block supplies constant power to neighboring components without a switch.
redstone_block.example: Place it beside a piston or powered rail to keep that component active.

redstone_torch.behavior: A redstone torch normally supplies power, but turns off when the block it is attached to is powered.
redstone_torch.example: Power its supporting block with a lever to invert the lever's on/off state.

repeater.behavior: A repeater carries a signal in one direction, restores its strength and adds an adjustable delay.
repeater.example: Point a repeater toward a lamp after a long dust line to extend the circuit.

comparator.behavior: A comparator reads signal strength or block state, then compares or subtracts its side input.
comparator.example: Place one facing away from a chest to read how full the chest is.

lever.behavior: A lever gives a steady signal until a player switches it off again.
lever.example: Use it as the on/off control for a redstone lamp.

stone_button.behavior: A stone button gives a short signal when pressed, then releases automatically.
stone_button.example: Connect it to a dispenser for one activation per press.

stone_pressure_plate.behavior: A stone pressure plate sends a signal while an entity stands on it.
stone_pressure_plate.example: Put one at an entrance to trigger a lamp or door as you pass.

daylight_detector.behavior: A daylight detector changes its output with skylight; its mode can be switched to react to darkness.
daylight_detector.example: Connect it to a lamp for lighting that follows the day and night cycle.

target.behavior: A target block gives a redstone signal when hit by a projectile; hits nearer the center are stronger.
target.example: Aim at the target to trigger a dispenser or open a practice-range gate.

observer.behavior: An observer watches the block in front of its face and emits a short pulse from its back when that block changes.
observer.example: Face it toward a growing crop and send its pulse to a piston.

sculk_sensor.behavior: A sculk sensor detects nearby vibrations and turns them into a redstone signal.
sculk_sensor.example: Connect one to a lamp to make a movement-sensitive indicator.

calibrated_sculk_sensor.behavior: A calibrated sculk sensor uses a signal on its input side to listen for a chosen vibration frequency.
calibrated_sculk_sensor.example: Feed its calibration side from a comparator, then connect its output to an alarm.

tripwire_hook.behavior: Two tripwire hooks joined by string emit a signal when something crosses the line.
tripwire_hook.example: Run the tripwire across a passage and connect a hook to a dispenser.

detector_rail.behavior: A detector rail sends a signal while a minecart is on it.
detector_rail.example: Place it before a junction to trigger a powered rail or station light.

piston.behavior: A piston extends when powered and pushes blocks in front of it.
piston.example: Power it through a lever to move a block into or out of a doorway.

sticky_piston.behavior: A sticky piston pushes a block when extending and can pull that block back when retracting.
sticky_piston.example: Use it with an observer to build a moving gate.

redstone_lamp.behavior: A redstone lamp lights up while it receives power.
redstone_lamp.example: Connect one to a lever, daylight detector or sensor for visible feedback.

dispenser.behavior: A dispenser activates an item from its inventory when it receives a pulse.
dispenser.example: Load arrows and trigger it with a button or tripwire.

dropper.behavior: A dropper ejects one item on a pulse or inserts it into a facing container.
dropper.example: Face it into a chest and pulse it to move items from a hopper-fed line.

note_block.behavior: A note block plays a tuned note when it receives a redstone pulse.
note_block.example: Set its pitch, then pulse it with a repeater for a simple rhythm.

tnt.behavior: A redstone signal primes TNT, starting its fuse before the explosion.
tnt.example: Use a button and a dust line to trigger it from a distance.

powered_rail.behavior: A powered rail accelerates a minecart while powered and slows it when unpowered.
powered_rail.example: Power a rail segment with a redstone block to keep a route moving.

activator_rail.behavior: An activator rail triggers a minecart's special behavior while the rail is powered.
activator_rail.example: Connect it to a detector rail to activate a passing minecart.

hopper.behavior: A hopper moves items between inventories; a redstone signal locks it and stops transfers.
hopper.example: Use a lever to pause a hopper line while you change the receiving container.

crafter.behavior: A crafter makes and ejects its current recipe when it receives a redstone pulse. Its input slots can be disabled.
crafter.example: Feed ingredients through hoppers and pulse the crafter with a button or clock.

speed.behavior: Increases movement speed while the effect lasts.
speed.obtain: Brew a Potion of Swiftness or choose Speed as a beacon power.
speed.tip: Useful for travel and dodging; higher levels make precise movement harder.

slowness.behavior: Reduces movement speed while the effect lasts.
slowness.obtain: Brew a Potion of Slowness or be hit by a stray's arrow.
slowness.tip: A milk bucket removes this effect, along with your other active effects.

jump_boost.behavior: Raises jump height and reduces some fall damage.
jump_boost.obtain: Brew a Potion of Leaping or choose Jump Boost as a beacon power.
jump_boost.tip: Use it to cross taller gaps; check your landing because it does not prevent all fall damage.

slow_falling.behavior: Slows falling and prevents fall damage while active.
slow_falling.obtain: Brew a Potion of Slow Falling with phantom membrane.
slow_falling.tip: Drink before gliding into a dangerous landing or dropping into a deep cave.

levitation.obtain: A shulker projectile applies Levitation on hit.
levitation.tip: Get beneath cover before it ends; the fall afterward can still hurt.

dolphins_grace.behavior: Makes swimming much faster near a dolphin in Java Edition.
dolphins_grace.obtain: Swim near a dolphin to receive the effect briefly.
dolphins_grace.tip: Combine it with underwater breathing for quicker ocean travel.

absorption.behavior: Adds temporary extra hearts that absorb damage before regular health.
absorption.obtain: Eat a golden apple or an enchanted golden apple.
absorption.tip: The extra hearts do not regenerate naturally; use them before a dangerous fight.

regeneration.obtain: Brew a Potion of Regeneration, eat a golden apple, or use a beacon's secondary power.
regeneration.tip: It helps between hits but cannot replace an instant heal during a burst of damage.

instant_health.behavior: Heals living targets immediately; it damages undead targets instead.
instant_health.obtain: Brew a Potion of Healing. Splash and lingering forms can affect other entities.
instant_health.tip: Throw a splash version at yourself for an immediate heal in combat.

instant_damage.behavior: Damages living targets immediately; it heals undead targets instead.
instant_damage.obtain: Brew a Potion of Harming from a healing or poison potion.
instant_damage.tip: Check the target: this effect is a poor choice against undead mobs.

poison.behavior: Deals damage over time but normally stops before killing the target.
poison.obtain: Brew a Potion of Poison, eat a spider eye or pufferfish, or take a cave spider hit.
poison.tip: Poison leaves you vulnerable at low health; recover before the next hit.

wither.behavior: Deals damage over time and can kill the affected entity.
wither.obtain: Wither skeleton attacks, the Wither boss, and wither roses can apply it.
wither.tip: Keep healing available: unlike ordinary Poison, Wither can finish you.

resistance.behavior: Reduces most incoming damage while the effect lasts.
resistance.obtain: Use a beacon, an enchanted golden apple, or a Potion of the Turtle Master.
resistance.tip: The Turtle Master potion also slows you heavily; plan your position first.

fire_resistance.behavior: Prevents damage from fire and lava while active.
fire_resistance.obtain: Brew a Potion of Fire Resistance or eat an enchanted golden apple.
fire_resistance.tip: Carry one when mining near lava; it will not prevent drowning or suffocation.

health_boost.behavior: Raises maximum health for the effect's duration.
health_boost.obtain: Health Boost has no standard survival source; it is available through commands.
health_boost.tip: When the effect ends, the extra maximum hearts disappear.

fatal_poison.behavior: A Bedrock-only poison variant that continues damaging until it can kill.
fatal_poison.obtain: Fatal Poison has no standard survival source; it can be applied with commands.
fatal_poison.tip: Treat it like Wither rather than ordinary Poison: it can reduce health to zero.

strength.obtain: Brew a Potion of Strength or choose Strength as a beacon power.
strength.tip: Use it before close-range fights; it does not make a bow shot stronger.

weakness.obtain: Brew a Potion of Weakness. A splash version is used when curing a zombie villager.
weakness.tip: Apply it to a zombie villager before giving a golden apple to begin the cure.

hunger.behavior: Makes the hunger bar drain faster during activity.
hunger.obtain: Eating rotten flesh, raw chicken or pufferfish can cause Hunger.
hunger.tip: Keep spare food nearby; the effect does not directly remove health.

saturation.behavior: Instantly restores food and hidden saturation points.
saturation.obtain: Certain suspicious stew recipes grant a brief Saturation effect.
saturation.tip: The effect is instant, so a short duration is enough to refill food.

haste.obtain: Choose Haste as a beacon's primary power.
haste.tip: Combine Haste with a suitable tool and Efficiency for faster mining.

mining_fatigue.obtain: An elder guardian applies Mining Fatigue around an ocean monument.
mining_fatigue.tip: Bring milk for a short removal window, then deal with the elder guardian.

infested.behavior: Gives a chance to spawn silverfish when the affected entity is hurt.
infested.obtain: Brew a Potion of Infestation or encounter an ominous trial effect.
infested.tip: Repeated hits can create extra threats around the target.

oozing.behavior: Spawns slimes when the affected entity dies.
oozing.obtain: Brew a Potion of Oozing or encounter an ominous trial effect.
oozing.tip: Leave space around the target before defeating it.

weaving.behavior: Spreads cobwebs when the affected entity dies and lets it move through webs faster.
weaving.obtain: Brew a Potion of Weaving or encounter an ominous trial effect.
weaving.tip: Webs can trap nearby players and mobs after the target dies.

wind_charged.behavior: Releases a wind burst when the affected entity dies.
wind_charged.obtain: Brew a Potion of Wind Charging or encounter an ominous trial effect.
wind_charged.tip: Keep your distance from the death burst and nearby ledges.

water_breathing.behavior: Prevents the air bar from running out underwater.
water_breathing.obtain: Brew a Potion of Water Breathing or wear a turtle helmet for a brief effect on entry.
water_breathing.tip: Use it for long dives; it does not improve swimming speed.

conduit_power.behavior: Provides underwater breathing, improved underwater mining and clearer vision near a conduit.
conduit_power.obtain: Activate a conduit in a prismarine frame and stay within its range.
conduit_power.tip: The conduit needs a valid surrounding frame to keep the effect active.

breath_of_the_nautilus.behavior: Pauses air consumption while riding a nautilus; it does not refill air.
breath_of_the_nautilus.obtain: Ride a nautilus or zombie nautilus underwater.
breath_of_the_nautilus.tip: Surface to refill your air before it runs out, then dive again.

night_vision.behavior: Brightens dark areas and improves visibility underwater.
night_vision.obtain: Brew a Potion of Night Vision with a golden carrot.
night_vision.tip: Useful in caves and oceans, but it does not protect against hostile mobs.

invisibility.behavior: Hides the affected entity's body, but held items and armor can remain visible.
invisibility.obtain: Brew a Potion of Invisibility from a night vision potion.
invisibility.tip: Remove visible equipment if you need to avoid being spotted.

blindness.behavior: Limits vision to a short area around the affected player.
blindness.obtain: Some suspicious stew recipes apply Blindness.
blindness.tip: Stop near cover rather than running into unseen terrain.

darkness.behavior: Pulses the player's vision dark around the deep dark's threats.
darkness.obtain: A sculk shrieker or Warden can apply Darkness nearby.
darkness.tip: Move quietly and use the pulse to find cover instead of rushing forward.

nausea.behavior: Distorts the screen while the effect lasts.
nausea.obtain: Eating a pufferfish can apply Nausea.
nausea.tip: Pause movement until your view settles; the visual distortion can hide hazards.

glowing.behavior: Shows an outline of the affected entity through blocks in Java Edition.
glowing.obtain: Hit an entity with a spectral arrow.
glowing.tip: Mark a moving target so you can track it behind cover.

bad_omen.behavior: Prepares an ominous event when the affected player reaches the right location.
bad_omen.obtain: Drink an ominous bottle in current releases; older releases grant it after defeating a raid captain.
bad_omen.tip: Entering a village or trial chamber while affected can change the encounter.

raid_omen.behavior: Counts down to an ominous raid after entering a village with Bad Omen.
raid_omen.obtain: Gain Bad Omen from an ominous bottle, then enter a village.
raid_omen.tip: Leave the village or clear the effect before the countdown ends if you are unprepared.

trial_omen.behavior: Makes a trial chamber's spawners and vaults ominous.
trial_omen.obtain: Enter a trial chamber with Bad Omen, usually from an ominous bottle.
trial_omen.tip: Expect a harder trial and prepare before activating spawners.

hero_of_the_village.behavior: Grants villager trade discounts after a successful raid defense.
hero_of_the_village.obtain: Defeat a raid to gain Hero of the Village.
hero_of_the_village.tip: Trade while the effect lasts to use the discounts.

luck.behavior: Raises the luck attribute used by some loot calculations in Java Edition.
luck.obtain: Luck has no standard survival source; commands or creative-only items can apply it.
luck.tip: It does not directly increase every drop rate.

unluck.behavior: Lowers the luck attribute used by some loot calculations in Java Edition.
unluck.obtain: Bad Luck has no standard survival source; commands can apply it.
unluck.tip: It affects only systems that consult the luck attribute.

smithingGuide.legacyUpgradeDescription: In this version, combine matching diamond gear and a Netherite Ingot directly at the smithing table. No template is required.

enchantmentSummaries.fire_protection: Reduces fire damage and burning duration.
enchantmentSummaries.frost_walker: Freezes water beneath your feet into temporary ice.
enchantmentSummaries.impaling: Deals extra trident damage to affected mobs.
enchantmentSummaries.infinity: Firing normal arrows does not consume them.
enchantmentSummaries.knockback: Pushes targets farther with melee hits.
enchantmentSummaries.looting: Improves eligible drops from defeated mobs.
enchantmentSummaries.loyalty: A thrown trident returns to its wielder.
enchantmentSummaries.luck_of_the_sea: Improves the chance of fishing up treasure.
enchantmentSummaries.lunge: A spear jab propels you forward while consuming hunger.
enchantmentSummaries.mending: Uses collected experience to repair the item.
enchantmentSummaries.multishot: Fires three projectiles from a crossbow at once.
enchantmentSummaries.piercing: Crossbow arrows pass through multiple targets.
enchantmentSummaries.respiration: Stay underwater longer before losing air.
enchantmentSummaries.riptide: Launches you with a trident in water or rain.
enchantmentSummaries.smite: Deals extra damage to undead mobs.
enchantmentSummaries.soul_speed: Move faster across soul sand and soul soil.
enchantmentSummaries.sweeping_edge: Increases damage to nearby targets of a sword sweep.
enchantmentSummaries.thorns: Attackers may take damage when they hit you.
enchantmentSummaries.unbreaking: Gives the item a chance to avoid durability loss.
enchantmentSummaries.vanishing_curse: The item disappears when its owner dies.
enchantmentSummaries.wind_burst: A mace smash launches you upward.

first-night.title: Survive your first night
first-night.summary: A practical route from your first log to tools, shelter, light, and food.

wood.title: Start with wood
wood.body: Break a tree, turn logs into planks, then make a crafting table. The table opens the larger grid needed for most early tools.

tools.title: Make basic tools
tools.body: Craft a wooden pickaxe to collect stone. Upgrade to a stone pickaxe before mining iron ore and keep spare blocks for a quick shelter.

shelter.title: Secure the night
shelter.body: Close off a small shelter before dark and light the area with torches. A bed lets you skip the night and sets your respawn point when used.

food.title: Build a food supply
food.body: Keep food on your hotbar. A furnace cooks raw meat, while bread gives you a renewable option once you have wheat.

mining.title: From stone to diamond
mining.summary: Gather ore safely, upgrade your pickaxe, and prepare for obsidian.

prepare.title: Pack for the cave
prepare.body: Take a pickaxe, torches, food, and spare blocks. Light passages as you go and avoid digging straight down into unseen space.

iron.title: Collect and smelt iron
iron.body: Mine raw iron with a suitable pickaxe, then smelt it in a furnace. Iron ingots unlock stronger tools and useful gear.

upgrade.title: Reach diamond
upgrade.body: Use an iron pickaxe to collect diamond ore. Craft a diamond pickaxe before attempting to mine obsidian.

obsidian.title: Collect obsidian
obsidian.body: Water meeting a lava source creates obsidian. Mine it with a diamond pickaxe and keep the water nearby to control exposed lava.

nether.title: Explore the Nether
nether.summary: Open a portal, prepare for hazards, and find the materials needed for brewing and the End.

portal.title: Open a portal
portal.body: Build an obsidian frame and light its interior with flint and steel. Bring the means to relight it if your return portal goes out.

prepare.title: Prepare for danger
prepare.body: Carry food and fire protection. Wearing one piece of gold armor keeps ordinary piglins neutral unless you provoke them; piglin brutes remain hostile.

fortress.title: Find a Nether fortress
fortress.body: Explore carefully around exposed bridges. Blazes drop rods that become blaze powder for brewing stands and Eyes of Ender.

wart.title: Bring back Nether wart
wart.body: Look for Nether wart in fortress stairwell gardens. Grow it on soul sand at home to maintain a brewing supply.

brewing.title: Brew your first potion
brewing.summary: Set up a brewing stand, make an Awkward Potion, then choose and modify an effect.

stand.title: Fuel the stand
stand.body: Place a brewing stand and load blaze powder into its fuel slot. Up to three bottles can be brewed together with one ingredient.

base.title: Make an Awkward Potion
base.body: Fill glass bottles with water. Brew Nether wart into the water bottles to make the base used by many useful potions.

effect.title: Choose an effect
effect.body: Brew an effect ingredient into the Awkward Potion. A glistering melon slice, for example, produces a Potion of Healing.

modify.title: Adjust the result
modify.body: Gunpowder turns a compatible potion into a throwable splash potion. Depending on the potion, redstone can extend duration or glowstone can strengthen its effect.

enchanting.title: Enchant your equipment
enchanting.summary: Use experience and lapis lazuli to improve gear, then combine useful enchantments.

table.title: Set up the table
table.body: Place an enchanting table and bring lapis lazuli and experience levels. The offered enchantments depend on the item and the available enchanting power.

bookshelves.title: Add bookshelves
bookshelves.body: Place bookshelves around the table with clear space between them. More valid shelves unlock stronger enchantment offers.

enchant.title: Pick a useful enchantment
enchant.body: Try an eligible tool and compare its offers. Efficiency improves mining speed; Unbreaking can reduce durability loss.

combine.title: Use an anvil
combine.body: Combine compatible enchanted gear or apply an enchanted book at an anvil. Check the experience cost before accepting the result.

trading.title: Trade with villagers
trading.summary: Find a village, choose a profession, earn emeralds, and unlock higher trade levels.

village.title: Find villagers
village.body: Villages are a natural starting point. Keep villagers safe and check each villager's profession before planning a trade route.

profession.title: Match a workstation
profession.body: An unemployed villager can take a profession from an available job site. A lectern creates a librarian, whose offers are shown in the trade guide.

emeralds.title: Earn emeralds
emeralds.body: Sell materials a villager wants, such as a farmer's crops. Prices and available offers can vary between villagers and change with demand or reputation.

advance.title: Unlock and restock
advance.body: Trading grants villager experience and unlocks higher levels. A villager needs access to its workstation to restock a used offer.

redstone.title: Build a redstone circuit
redstone.summary: Connect a power source to a device, then add timing and simple item movement.

power.title: Start with a switch
power.body: Use a lever as an on/off power source. Lay redstone dust to carry its signal toward a device.

output.title: Connect an output
output.body: Power a redstone lamp for an obvious test, then try a piston to move a block. Check how each component faces when placed.

timing.title: Control the signal
timing.body: A repeater can refresh a signal and add a delay. A comparator reads or compares signal strength for more selective circuits.

automation.title: Move and dispense items
automation.body: Use a hopper to transfer items between containers. A dispenser acts when powered and behaves differently depending on its contents.

the-end.title: Reach the End
the-end.summary: Gather Eyes of Ender, find a stronghold, and prepare for the Ender Dragon.

pearls.title: Gather Ender Pearls
pearls.body: Endermen are one source of Ender Pearls. Bring food and suitable gear before gathering what you need.

powder.title: Get blaze powder
powder.body: Find a Nether fortress and collect blaze rods. Turn them into blaze powder to combine with Ender Pearls.

stronghold.title: Locate the stronghold
stronghold.body: Craft Eyes of Ender and follow their direction toward a stronghold. Bring extra eyes to activate any empty End portal frames.

dragon.title: Prepare for the dragon
dragon.body: Take ranged and melee weapons, food, and fall protection. Destroy the End Crystals that heal the dragon before focusing on the fight.

wither.title: Defeat the Wither
wither.summary: Collect summoning materials, prepare an arena, and turn the Nether Star into a beacon.

skulls.title: Collect three skulls
skulls.body: Fight Wither Skeletons in Nether fortresses until you have three skulls. Bring four blocks of soul sand or soul soil for the body.

summon.title: Choose an arena
summon.body: Build the T-shaped body and place the three skulls last. Summon the Wither away from valuable builds and stand clear while it charges.

fight.title: Survive the fight
fight.body: Bring strong weapons, healing, and a way to remove the Wither effect. Watch for the Wither's second phase, when ranged attacks become ineffective.

beacon.title: Use the Nether Star
beacon.body: Defeating the Wither drops a Nether Star. Craft a beacon and place it above a valid mineral-block pyramid to activate its effects.

tradeGuide.professionIntro: Possible base offers for this profession in the selected edition and version. Each villager has a selection; prices can change.
tradeGuide.wanderingIntro: Possible base trades for the wandering trader in this edition and version. Each trader offers a selection and does not restock.
tradeGuide.offerIntro: A base trade from the selected edition and version. Actual prices can vary.

blockGuide.surfaceCaveat: These biomes feature this block in natural terrain; it can occur elsewhere too.
blockGuide.surfaceSummary: This block occurs naturally in some biomes. Explore where it appears below.

ore.processingNote: An intact ore block can also be smelted; see the result below.
ore.smeltedProcessingNote: Smelt the mined block to obtain the result. Open it for stations and timing.
ore.miningTip: Mine with a suitable pickaxe. Fortune can increase the resource yield; Silk Touch collects the ore block instead.
ore.smeltedMiningTip: Mine the buried block with a suitable pickaxe. The block itself drops; Fortune does not increase it.
ore.deepslateTip: The deepslate variant takes longer to break.

summary.button: A wooden switch made from matching planks.
summary.pressurePlate: A wooden floor switch made from matching planks.
summary.trapdoor: A hinged wooden hatch made from matching planks.

behavior.button: Press it to send a brief redstone signal. Wooden buttons can also be activated by arrows.
behavior.pressurePlate: Entities and dropped items on the plate power it. The signal stops after they leave.
behavior.trapdoor: Open or close it by hand, or control it with a redstone signal.

bedrock.location: Forms the bottom boundary of the Overworld and both the floor and ceiling of the Nether.
bedrock.survival: It cannot be mined or collected in Survival. Creative mode can place and break it.

end_portal_frame.location: Generates in the portal room of a stronghold. The frame itself cannot be collected in Survival.
end_portal_frame.use: Fill the empty frame blocks with Eyes of Ender to activate the End portal.

budding_amethyst.location: Found inside underground amethyst geodes. Breaking it destroys the block, even with Silk Touch.
budding_amethyst.use: Amethyst buds grow on exposed sides and mature into clusters. Harvest the clusters for amethyst shards.

highlights.grass_block: Grass spreads over nearby dirt when conditions allow. Breaking this block without Silk Touch drops dirt; Silk Touch preserves it.
highlights.sand: A falling terrain block found in dry and coastal areas. Smelt it into glass or craft sandstone.
highlights.red_sand: The red sand of the badlands. It falls when unsupported and can be smelted into glass.
highlights.mycelium: The ground cover of mushroom fields. It can spread to nearby dirt; Silk Touch collects the block itself.
highlights.sculk: Sculk grows around sculk catalysts in the deep dark. Mining it without Silk Touch yields experience instead of the block.
highlights.crafting_table: Opens a 3×3 crafting grid for recipes that do not fit in your inventory.
highlights.furnace: Smelts items using fuel. Blast furnaces process ores faster, while smokers cook food faster.
highlights.smithing_table: Combines templates, gear and materials for netherite upgrades and armor trims.
highlights.brewing_stand: Brews potions from bottles and ingredients, using blaze powder as fuel.
highlights.enchanting_table: Uses experience and lapis lazuli to enchant equipment. Nearby bookshelves unlock higher enchantment levels.
highlights.obsidian: A hard block used to build Nether portals. Collect it with a diamond or netherite pickaxe.
highlights.ancient_debris: A rare Nether ore that smelts into netherite scrap. It resists normal explosions.
highlights.bedrock: An unbreakable Survival boundary block. It defines the bottom of the Overworld and the floor and roof of the Nether.
highlights.end_portal_frame: The stronghold portal frame that opens a path to the End when filled with Eyes of Ender.
highlights.budding_amethyst: A geode block that grows amethyst buds and clusters; leave it intact to keep harvesting crystals.

biomeGuide.unavailable: Biome data is unavailable for this edition and version.
biomeGuide.climateNote: Temperature and downfall are game data values, not °C or a rain percentage.
biomeGuide.landmarkNote: These structures can generate in this biome; terrain and world generation still affect their placement.

highlights.badlands: Red sand and layered terracotta shape this dry biome. Look for plentiful gold ore and exposed mineshafts.
highlights.deep_dark: Sculk covers this underground biome. Ancient cities can generate here; noise can alert the Warden.
highlights.dappled_forest: A forest of red, orange and yellow poplars near cold biomes. Look for shelf mushrooms, red shrubs and abandoned camps.

families.forests: A forest or wooded biome with its own climate, terrain and mob spawns.
families.meadows: An open landscape; climate and mob spawns vary across this biome family.
families.oceans: A water or shore biome with its own climate and aquatic life.
families.mountains: A mountain or cave biome shaped by its climate and terrain.
families.deserts: A dry biome where terrain and generation create distinct landmarks.
families.nether: A Nether biome with distinct terrain and hostile mob spawns.
families.end: An End biome with terrain and structures unique to this dimension.

summaries.allay: Give an allay an item and it will collect matching dropped items. A nearby note block can become its delivery point.
summaries.armadillo: Armadillos curl up when startled. Brush one or wait for a shed scute to collect material for wolf armor.
summaries.axolotl: Axolotls live in lush-cave water and attack many aquatic mobs. Helping one in a fight can give you a brief regeneration effect.
summaries.bat: Bats fly through dark caves and rest upside down. They do not attack or provide a useful drop.
summaries.bee: Bees collect pollen from flowers, pollinate crops and return to their nests to make honey.
summaries.blaze: Blazes guard Nether fortresses and attack with volleys of fireballs. Their rods are needed for brewing and reaching the End.
summaries.bogged: This swamp skeleton shoots poisonous arrows. Shearing it removes its mushrooms; defeat it for its usual skeleton loot.
summaries.breeze: The breeze appears in trial chambers and attacks with wind charges that knock targets around and trigger some blocks.
summaries.camel_husk: Camel husks roam deserts and may carry hostile undead riders. The mount itself is passive and can be claimed after its riders are defeated.
summaries.camel: Camels are tall desert mounts that carry two players. Their dash crosses gaps, and their height keeps many short enemies out of reach.
summaries.cat: Cats can be tamed with raw fish. They scare away creepers and phantoms, and a sleeping tamed cat may bring a morning gift.
summaries.cave_spider: Cave spiders appear around mineshaft spawners. They fit through narrow gaps and can poison players they bite.
summaries.chicken: Chickens lay eggs over time and drop feathers and meat when killed. Seeds can be used to breed them.
summaries.cod: Cod swim in oceans and can be collected in buckets. They provide raw cod when caught or defeated.
summaries.copper_golem: A copper golem moves items from copper chests into nearby ordinary chests. It slowly oxidizes unless waxed.
summaries.cow: Cows graze in the Overworld. Use a bucket for milk, breed them with wheat, or obtain beef and leather on defeat.
summaries.creaking: The creaking stalks players in pale gardens when they look away. Locate and break its connected creaking heart to stop it.
summaries.creeper: Creepers approach quietly and explode after getting close. Keep your distance or interrupt the approach with knockback.
summaries.dolphin: Dolphins swim in oceans and can boost a nearby swimmer's speed. Feeding one raw fish can lead you toward an underwater structure.
summaries.donkey: Donkeys can be tamed and ridden. Equip a chest to carry items while travelling.
summaries.drowned: Drowned are underwater zombies that may carry tridents or nautilus shells. Zombies can also convert after remaining submerged.
summaries.elder_guardian: An elder guardian protects an ocean monument. Its laser and Mining Fatigue effect make underwater preparation important.
summaries.ender_dragon: The Ender Dragon circles the central island and heals from end crystals. Destroy the crystals before finishing the fight.
summaries.enderman: Endermen teleport and carry some blocks. Avoid looking directly at one unless you are ready to fight.
summaries.endermite: An endermite can appear when an ender pearl is used. It attacks nearby players and attracts endermen.
summaries.evoker: Evokers use fang attacks and summon vexes. They are encountered in woodland mansions and raids.
summaries.fox: Foxes roam taiga biomes, pick up items and hunt small animals. Sweet berries or glow berries can be used to breed them.
summaries.frog: Frogs eat small slimes and magma cubes. The magma cube meal creates a froglight whose color depends on the frog variant.
summaries.ghast: Ghasts float through the Nether and fire explosive fireballs. A well-timed hit can send a fireball back.
summaries.giant: The giant is an unused oversized zombie. It does not appear naturally and can only be summoned with commands.
summaries.glow_squid: Glow squids swim in dark underground water and release glow ink sacs when defeated. The ink can make sign text glow.
summaries.goat: Goats live on mountain slopes and may ram nearby mobs or players. A ram into a suitable hard block can leave a goat horn.
summaries.guardian: Guardians patrol ocean monuments and fire a charging laser. Their spikes also punish close attacks while extended.
summaries.happy_ghast: Raise a dried ghast into a happy ghast, then equip a harness for a flying mount that can carry several players.
summaries.hoglin: Hoglins are aggressive Nether animals found in crimson forests. They fear warped fungi and can be bred with crimson fungi.
summaries.horse: Horses can be tamed, saddled and ridden across the Overworld. Individuals vary in speed, jump height and health.
summaries.husk: Husks are desert zombies that do not burn in sunlight. Their melee attacks can inflict Hunger.
summaries.illusioner: The illusioner is a command-only illager. It attacks with a bow, uses blindness and creates decoy images.
summaries.iron_golem: Iron golems defend villagers from hostile mobs. They can also be built by players using iron blocks and a carved pumpkin.
summaries.llama: Llamas can carry chests and form caravans when led. They spit at attackers and can be bred with hay bales.
summaries.magma_cube: Magma cubes jump through the Nether and split into smaller cubes when defeated. Their size changes the threat and drops.
summaries.mooshroom: Mooshrooms live on mushroom fields. Use a bowl for mushroom stew, milk them with a bucket, or shear one into a cow.
summaries.mule: A mule is bred from a horse and a donkey. It can be ridden and fitted with a chest, but cannot breed itself.
summaries.nautilus: Nautiluses swim in oceans and can be tamed and bred with pufferfish. Riding one preserves your air supply underwater.
summaries.ocelot: Ocelots live in jungles and flee from players. Raw fish can earn their trust, but they do not become pet cats.
summaries.panda: Pandas roam bamboo jungles and eat bamboo. Their personalities affect behavior, and a sneeze can leave a slimeball.
summaries.parched: The parched is a desert skeleton that stays active in sunlight. It attacks from range and can ride a camel husk.
summaries.parrot: Parrots live in jungles and can be tamed with seeds. They mimic nearby hostile mobs and can perch on your shoulder.
summaries.phantom: Phantoms swoop at players who have gone several in-game days without sleep. Sleeping prevents their natural appearance.
summaries.pig: Pigs are passive farm animals that provide porkchops. Breed them with vegetables, or ride one with a saddle and carrot on a stick.
summaries.piglin_brute: Piglin brutes guard bastion remnants. They attack on sight and cannot be distracted by gold.
summaries.piglin: Piglins roam the Nether and become hostile toward players without gold armor. Offer a gold ingot to barter with an adult.
summaries.pillager: Pillagers attack with crossbows. They appear in patrols, at outposts and during raids.
summaries.polar_bear: Polar bears roam icy biomes. Adults retaliate when attacked and become dangerous near cubs.
summaries.pufferfish: Pufferfish inflate when threatened and can poison nearby players. They can also be caught in a bucket.
summaries.rabbit: Rabbits hop through several Overworld biomes and flee from players. Breed them with carrots, golden carrots or dandelions.
summaries.ravager: Ravagers are powerful raid beasts that charge through obstacles and strike in melee. Keep space between yourself and their rider.
summaries.salmon: Salmon swim in rivers and colder oceans. They can be caught in a bucket and provide raw salmon as food.
summaries.sheep: Sheep grow wool that can be sheared repeatedly. Breed them with wheat to expand a flock.
summaries.shulker: Shulkers hide as blocks in End cities and fire projectiles that cause Levitation. Their shells are used for shulker boxes.
summaries.silverfish: Silverfish hide in infested blocks and emerge when those blocks break. Attacking one can call nearby silverfish.
summaries.skeleton_horse: Skeleton horses can appear in a lightning-triggered trap. Once acquired, they can be saddled and ridden.
summaries.skeleton: Skeletons attack from range with bows and burn in daylight. A shield or cover helps against their arrows.
summaries.slime: Slimes jump in swamps and slime chunks. Large ones split when defeated; small ones provide slimeballs.
summaries.sniffer: Sniffers hatch from eggs and dig ancient seeds out of the ground. Use torchflower seeds to breed them.
summaries.snow_golem: Snow golems throw snowballs at hostile mobs and leave snow trails where the climate allows. They can be built from snow and a carved pumpkin.
summaries.spider: Spiders climb walls and usually attack in darkness. In bright light they are normally neutral unless provoked.
summaries.squid: Squids swim in rivers and oceans. They release ink sacs when defeated.
summaries.stray: Strays are cold-biome skeletons whose arrows inflict Slowness. They can also result from a skeleton freezing in powder snow.
summaries.strider: Striders walk across lava in the Nether. Saddle one and steer it with a warped fungus on a stick.
summaries.sulfur_cube: Sulfur cubes absorb blocks and take on their physical properties, from bouncing or sliding to explosive behavior.
summaries.tadpole: Tadpoles hatch from frogspawn and grow into frogs. The biome where they mature determines their frog variant.
summaries.trader_llama: Trader llamas accompany wandering traders and defend themselves by spitting. They can later be equipped with chests.
summaries.tropical_fish: Tropical fish swim in warm oceans in many color and pattern variants. They can be carried in buckets.
summaries.turtle: Turtles return to their home beach to lay eggs. Their young leave scutes as they grow, and seagrass breeds adults.
summaries.vex: Vexes are small flying attackers summoned by evokers. They can pass through blocks and pursue targets for a limited time.
summaries.villager: Villagers live in villages and take jobs from workstations. Trade with them to exchange goods for emeralds and other items.
summaries.vindicator: Vindicators are axe-wielding illagers found in woodland mansions and raids. They rush into close combat.
summaries.wandering_trader: Wandering traders appear with two trader llamas and offer a rotating selection of items for emeralds.
summaries.warden: The warden emerges in the deep dark when sculk shriekers are triggered. It tracks vibrations and scent, then attacks at close range or with a sonic boom.
summaries.witch: Witches use harmful splash potions and drink defensive potions. They can appear in swamps, witch huts and raids.
summaries.wither_skeleton: Wither skeletons patrol Nether fortresses with stone swords. Their hits inflict Wither, and their skulls are needed to summon the Wither.
summaries.wither: The Wither is a player-summoned boss that fires explosive skulls and inflicts Wither. At half health it blocks projectiles.
summaries.wolf: Wolves can be tamed with bones and will defend their owner. Breed tamed wolves with meat.
summaries.zoglin: Zoglins result when hoglins enter the Overworld. They attack many nearby mobs and cannot be bred.
summaries.zombie_horse: Zombie horses can appear in the Overworld at night. Defeat any hostile rider to claim and saddle the mount.
summaries.zombie_nautilus: Zombie nautiluses appear underwater, often with a trident-wielding drowned rider. Remove the rider and use pufferfish to tame the mount.
summaries.zombie_villager: Zombie villagers attack like zombies, but a Weakness effect and golden apple can cure one back into a villager.
summaries.zombie: Zombies pursue players and villagers, can call reinforcements and usually burn in sunlight. Keep distance or use cover.
summaries.zombified_piglin: Zombified piglins roam the Nether and remain neutral until attacked. Hitting one can anger others nearby.

habitats.allay: Cages at pillager outposts and rooms in woodland mansions.
habitats.axolotl: Water in lush caves, above clay blocks.
habitats.bat: Dark cave spaces in the Overworld.
habitats.bee: Bee nests attached to trees in meadows, plains and forest biomes with flowers.
habitats.blaze: Nether fortresses, especially near blaze spawners.
habitats.bogged: Swamps and mangrove swamps; also some trial chamber encounters.
habitats.breeze: Trial chamber spawners in the Overworld.
habitats.camel_husk: Desert terrain, sometimes carrying husk or parched riders.
habitats.camel: Desert villages and other suitable desert terrain.
habitats.cat: Villages, with black cats also appearing around swamp huts.
habitats.cave_spider: Mineshaft cave-spider spawners, usually behind cobwebs.
habitats.chicken: Grassy Overworld biomes and player farms.
habitats.cod: Ocean waters outside the warmest tropical areas.
habitats.copper_golem: Created by players from a copper block and a carved pumpkin.
habitats.cow: Grassy Overworld biomes and player farms.
habitats.creaking: Pale gardens at night, linked to a nearby creaking heart.
habitats.creeper: Dark Overworld areas and unlit caves.
habitats.dolphin: Ocean waters, usually in groups near the surface.
habitats.donkey: Open grassland biomes such as plains and savannas.
habitats.drowned: Oceans and rivers; also created when a zombie stays underwater.
habitats.elder_guardian: Inside ocean monuments, with a limited number per monument.
habitats.ender_dragon: The central island of the End dimension.
habitats.enderman: The End, plus dark areas of the Overworld and Nether.
habitats.endermite: Occasionally created by a thrown ender pearl.
habitats.evoker: Woodland mansions and some village raids.
habitats.frog: Swamps and mangrove swamps; tadpoles can grow elsewhere.
habitats.giant: No natural spawn; available through commands.
habitats.glow_squid: Dark underground water in the Overworld.
habitats.guardian: Ocean monuments and the surrounding waters.
habitats.happy_ghast: Raised from a dried ghast rather than found naturally as an adult.
habitats.hoglin: Crimson forests and some bastion remnants in the Nether.
habitats.husk: Deserts and other hot, dry Overworld areas.
habitats.illusioner: No natural spawn; available through commands.
habitats.iron_golem: Villages or a player-built iron-block structure.
habitats.llama: Windswept hills and savanna plateau terrain.
habitats.mule: Bred from a horse and donkey; does not spawn naturally.
habitats.panda: Bamboo jungles and nearby jungle terrain.
habitats.phantom: Night skies above players who have not slept for several days.
habitats.pig: Grassy Overworld biomes and player farms.
habitats.piglin: Nether wastes, crimson forests and bastion remnants.
habitats.pillager: Pillager outposts, patrols and village raids.
habitats.polar_bear: Snowy plains and icy coastal biomes.
habitats.rabbit: Several Overworld biomes, including deserts and snowy areas.
habitats.sheep: Grassy Overworld biomes and player farms.
habitats.shulker: End cities, attached to purpur surfaces.
habitats.skeleton: Dark Overworld areas and unlit caves.
habitats.slime: Swamps and special underground slime chunks.
habitats.sniffer: Hatched from a sniffer egg found by brushing warm ocean ruins.
habitats.snow_golem: Built by players from snow blocks and a carved pumpkin.
habitats.spider: Dark Overworld areas and unlit caves.
habitats.squid: Rivers and oceans in the Overworld.
habitats.stray: Cold biomes; also created when a skeleton freezes in powder snow.
habitats.sulfur_cube: Sulfur caves underground in the Overworld.
habitats.tadpole: Hatched from frogspawn placed on water.
habitats.tropical_fish: Warm and lukewarm oceans, often near coral reefs.
habitats.vex: Summoned by an evoker during combat.
habitats.villager: Overworld villages, or bred by players with beds and food.
habitats.wandering_trader: Appears periodically near players with two trader llamas.
habitats.warden: Deep dark areas after repeated sculk-shrieker warnings.
habitats.witch: Dark Overworld spaces, swamp huts and some raids.
habitats.wither: Summoned by placing wither-skeleton skulls on soul sand or soul soil.
habitats.wolf: Forests, taigas, groves and other suitable Overworld biomes.
habitats.zoglin: Created when a hoglin stays outside the Nether.
habitats.zombie_horse: Can appear at night; older releases require commands.
habitats.zombie_nautilus: Oceans, often with a drowned rider.
habitats.zombie_villager: Dark Overworld areas or when a villager is infected by a zombie.
habitats.zombie: Dark Overworld areas and unlit caves.
habitats.zombified_piglin: Nether wastes and other Nether areas; also around Nether portals.

interactions.allay: Hand it an item to set what it collects; use a note block to redirect deliveries.
interactions.armadillo: Brush an armadillo for scutes, or wait for it to shed one naturally.
interactions.axolotl: Carry one in a water bucket and release it near an underwater fight.
interactions.bat: Bats cannot be tamed or bred and have no direct item drops.
interactions.bee: Bees visit flowers for pollen and fertilize crops as they fly back to a nest or hive.
interactions.blaze: Blaze rods fuel brewing stands and craft blaze powder; bring fire protection for a fortress trip.
interactions.bogged: Shear a bogged to collect mushrooms before defeating it.
interactions.breeze: Wind charges from a defeated breeze can be used for movement and activating compatible blocks.
interactions.camel_husk: Remove its hostile riders before approaching; the remaining mount can be saddled and ridden.
interactions.camel: Saddle a camel for up to two riders. Use its charged dash to cross gaps.
interactions.cat: Approach carefully with raw cod or salmon to tame; a tamed cat may leave a gift after you sleep.
interactions.cave_spider: Destroy or secure the mineshaft spawner to stop repeated cave-spider attacks.
interactions.chicken: Use seeds to breed chickens; collect the eggs they lay without harming them.
interactions.cod: Use a water bucket to move a live cod; raw cod can be cooked for food.
interactions.copper_golem: Place items in a copper chest for sorting; wax the golem to prevent it becoming a statue.
interactions.cow: Use a bucket for renewable milk, and wheat to breed more cows.
interactions.creaking: Follow the particles between a struck creaking and its heart, then break the heart block.
interactions.creeper: A cat can deter creepers; their explosion can be blocked or avoided by keeping distance.
interactions.dolphin: Swim nearby for Dolphin's Grace; feed raw fish to make one lead you toward a structure.
interactions.donkey: Tame by riding until it accepts you, then saddle it and add a chest for storage.
interactions.drowned: Check what it is holding: a naturally spawned drowned can carry a trident or nautilus shell.
interactions.elder_guardian: Bring water breathing and a plan for Mining Fatigue before entering the monument.
interactions.ender_dragon: Break or shoot end crystals first so the dragon cannot heal from them.
interactions.enderman: Avoid eye contact; a carved pumpkin prevents accidental provocation by looking.
interactions.endermite: An endermite can be used to attract endermen in a controlled farm.
interactions.evoker: Defeating an evoker yields a totem of undying; watch for summoned vexes.
interactions.fox: Breed two foxes with berries; the baby trusts the player who bred it.
interactions.frog: Feed small magma cubes to frogs for froglights; tadpoles grow into variants based on climate.
interactions.ghast: Strike a ghast fireball to send it back toward the ghast.
interactions.giant: This command-only mob has no normal survival encounter or regular AI behavior.
interactions.glow_squid: Use glow ink sacs to make sign text and item-frame contents glow.
interactions.goat: Stand near a suitable hard block, then dodge a goat's charge to obtain a horn.
interactions.guardian: Clear the guardians before mining or exploring an ocean monument.
interactions.happy_ghast: Equip a harness to carry several players through the air.
interactions.hoglin: Use warped fungus to repel hoglins; crimson fungus breeds them.
interactions.horse: Tame by riding, then saddle it; breed tamed horses with golden food.
interactions.husk: Husks do not burn in sunlight, so daytime is not a safe escape.
interactions.illusioner: This mob is available through commands rather than a normal survival encounter.
interactions.iron_golem: Build one to defend a settlement, but avoid hitting a naturally spawned village golem.
interactions.llama: A leashed llama can lead a caravan; equip chests for transport.
interactions.magma_cube: Small magma cubes can provide magma cream for fire-resistance brewing.
interactions.mooshroom: Use a bowl for stew or shear a mooshroom to obtain mushrooms and an ordinary cow.
interactions.mule: Crossbreed a horse and a donkey, then equip the mule with a saddle and chest.
interactions.nautilus: Tame and breed with pufferfish, then saddle it for underwater travel without using up your air.
interactions.ocelot: Feed raw fish until it trusts you; trust stops it fleeing but does not make it a pet cat.
interactions.panda: Provide bamboo near the pair to breed pandas; a sneezing baby may leave a slimeball.
interactions.parched: Use cover against its bow, even during the day when ordinary skeletons would burn.
interactions.parrot: Tame with seeds and listen for its mimicry as a warning of nearby hostile mobs.
interactions.phantom: Sleep in a bed to reset the insomnia that allows phantoms to appear.
interactions.pig: Breed pigs with carrots, potatoes or beetroots; use a saddle and carrot on a stick to ride one.
interactions.piglin_brute: Gold armor and gold ingots do not pacify a piglin brute.
interactions.piglin: Wear gold armor to avoid an immediate attack; offer gold ingots to barter with adults.
interactions.pillager: A shield can stop crossbow bolts while you close the distance.
interactions.polar_bear: Keep away from cubs and avoid striking adults to prevent a bear attack.
interactions.pufferfish: Collect one with a water bucket while staying clear of its inflated poison radius.
interactions.rabbit: Use carrots, golden carrots or dandelions to breed rabbits.
interactions.ravager: Fight from cover or elevation and watch for an illager riding the ravager.
interactions.salmon: Catch one in a water bucket, or cook its drop for food.
interactions.sheep: Use shears for renewable wool; dye a sheep before shearing for colored wool.
interactions.shulker: Collect shulker shells to craft shulker boxes with portable storage.
interactions.silverfish: Mining infested blocks can release silverfish; secure the area before clearing them.
interactions.skeleton_horse: After surviving the skeleton trap, saddle the horse for a rideable undead mount.
interactions.skeleton: Use a shield to block arrows or force the skeleton into close combat.
interactions.slime: Small slimes provide slimeballs for leads, sticky pistons and other recipes.
interactions.sniffer: Plant its torchflower and pitcher seeds, and use torchflower seeds to breed sniffers.
interactions.snow_golem: Build one for ranged distraction; keep it out of hot biomes where it melts.
interactions.spider: Wait for daylight or light the area to stop an unprovoked spider from hunting you.
interactions.squid: Ink sacs from squids can make black dye and writable-book materials.
interactions.stray: Carry a shield or use cover to avoid Slowness arrows.
interactions.strider: Saddle it, then steer with warped fungus on a stick to cross lava.
interactions.sulfur_cube: Offer a block to change its physics; use shears to remove the block. Small cubes grow when fed slimeballs, and large ones fit in an empty bucket.
interactions.tadpole: Move one in a water bucket and choose its maturation biome for the desired frog variant.
interactions.trader_llama: Trader llamas can defend the trader and may be equipped with chests after separation.
interactions.tropical_fish: Catch a preferred color variant in a water bucket for transport or an aquarium.
interactions.turtle: Protect the eggs on their home beach; growing young turtles leave scutes.
interactions.vex: Focus on the evoker summoning vexes, then keep moving to avoid their attacks through walls.
interactions.villager: Place workstations for professions and trade repeatedly to unlock more offers.
interactions.vindicator: Keep range or use a shield against its fast axe attacks.
interactions.wandering_trader: Check the limited-time offers before the trader despawns.
interactions.warden: Avoid triggering shriekers, crouch to reduce vibrations and leave instead of fighting.
interactions.witch: Witches heal and resist damage with potions; close the gap between throws.
interactions.wither_skeleton: Collect three skulls to summon the Wither; a shield helps against sword hits.
interactions.wither: Prepare an open arena and fight with ranged weapons until its projectile shield activates.
interactions.wolf: Tame with bones and breed tamed wolves with meat. Some newer versions also support wolf armor.
interactions.zoglin: Keep a converted zoglin contained: it attacks most other mobs nearby.
interactions.zombie_horse: Once the rider is removed, saddle the zombie horse for travel.
interactions.zombie_nautilus: Remove the drowned rider, then use pufferfish to tame and saddle the mount.
interactions.zombie_villager: Apply Weakness and feed a golden apple to start curing it.
interactions.zombie: Keep villagers sheltered; zombies can infect them and may break doors on hard difficulty.
interactions.zombified_piglin: Avoid striking one unless ready for nearby zombified piglins to join the fight.

combatTips.bee: Hitting a bee, breaking its nest or taking honey without smoke can provoke nearby bees to swarm.
combatTips.blaze: Break line of sight during fireball volleys, then attack between bursts. Fire Resistance reduces the danger.
combatTips.bogged: Poison arrows are the main threat. Block them with a shield and close the gap.
combatTips.breeze: Watch for wind-charge knockback near ledges; time hits between its quick leaps.
combatTips.cave_spider: Block narrow passages and bring a way to deal with Poison before entering a mineshaft nest.
combatTips.creaking: Weapon hits do not end the encounter. Keep it in view while finding and breaking the connected heart.
combatTips.creeper: Back away as it begins to hiss. The explosion is strongest up close and can damage terrain.
combatTips.dolphin: Normally harmless, but a dolphin retaliates if struck and nearby dolphins may join in.
combatTips.drowned: A drowned holding a trident can attack at range underwater; use cover and close carefully.
combatTips.elder_guardian: Its laser needs time to charge. Break line of sight, then attack while avoiding spikes and Mining Fatigue.
combatTips.enderman: Eye contact or an attack provokes it. Water and low ceilings can protect you from its reach and teleporting.
combatTips.endermite: It is small and quick; clear it before fighting nearby endermen.
combatTips.evoker: Avoid the line of fang attacks and eliminate summoned vexes before they surround you.
combatTips.ghast: Use a bow or return its fireball; keep solid cover between volleys.
combatTips.goat: A goat may ram suddenly. Watch its charging stance and sidestep near a hard block.
combatTips.guardian: Interrupt its laser by moving behind cover; extended spikes hurt melee attackers.
combatTips.hoglin: Its charge and knockback are dangerous near lava. Warped fungus creates a safer gap.
combatTips.husk: A hit adds Hunger. Unlike a zombie, a husk will remain active in daylight.
combatTips.illusioner: Blindness and illusory copies make target selection difficult; track the real archer.
combatTips.iron_golem: Do not provoke a village golem at close range; its upward strike deals heavy damage.
combatTips.llama: A llama spits when attacked, so give it space if you accidentally hit it.
combatTips.magma_cube: Large cubes split into smaller attackers. Keep room to move and clear each wave.
combatTips.nautilus: A wild nautilus can dash at attackers; leave it alone or tame it with pufferfish.
combatTips.panda: A panda usually ignores players but can retaliate after being hit.
combatTips.parched: Arrows remain a threat in full sunlight; fight from cover or use a shield.
combatTips.phantom: Listen for its call, face the incoming swoop and hit as it descends.
combatTips.piglin_brute: Brutes attack even through gold armor and cannot barter. Keep a safe retreat route in bastions.
combatTips.piglin: Gold armor prevents ordinary aggression, but opening containers or mining gold nearby can anger piglins.
combatTips.pillager: Shield the crossbow shot, then advance during the reload.
combatTips.polar_bear: Adults near cubs can attack without being struck. Stay clear of the family group.
combatTips.pufferfish: Its inflated body poisons nearby players on contact; do not crowd it underwater.
combatTips.ravager: Its melee hits and knockback are strong. Use range or terrain to avoid a direct charge.
combatTips.shulker: Levitation bullets can lift you into dangerous falls. Keep a roof overhead and hit when the shell opens.
combatTips.silverfish: Damaging one can rouse others from infested blocks. Avoid breaking nearby blocks mid-fight.
combatTips.skeleton: A shield blocks arrows; nearby cover interrupts its line of sight.
combatTips.slime: Only the smallest slimes are harmless. Larger ones hit harder and split when defeated.
combatTips.spider: It can climb vertical walls and leap at you; bright conditions reduce unprovoked attacks.
combatTips.stray: Its arrows apply Slowness, making escape harder. Use a shield and close the distance.
combatTips.sulfur_cube: Normally passive, but absorbed TNT can ignite and an absorbed magma block can harm nearby entities.
combatTips.trader_llama: A trader llama may spit in retaliation after being attacked.
combatTips.vex: Vexes fly through blocks, so walls will not stop them. Keep moving and target the summoning evoker.
combatTips.vindicator: An axe hit is dangerous at close range. Use reach or knockback to keep distance.
combatTips.warden: Sneaking reduces vibration, but the warden can still smell you and use a sonic boom through obstacles.
combatTips.witch: Splash potions can poison or slow you. Attack between throws and avoid lingering near the witch.
combatTips.wither_skeleton: The Wither effect continues after a sword hit. Bring healing and keep enough room to retreat.
combatTips.wolf: A wild wolf fights back when struck and may draw nearby wolves into the attack.
combatTips.zoglin: A zoglin attacks many creatures around it. Contain it before it reaches a settlement.
combatTips.zombie_nautilus: Its drowned rider can throw tridents; separate or defeat the rider before approaching the mount.
combatTips.zombie_villager: It attacks like a zombie. Trap it safely before attempting the cure.
combatTips.zombie: Watch for groups and possible reinforcements; daylight usually burns exposed zombies.
combatTips.zombified_piglin: One accidental hit can turn a neutral group hostile. Avoid sweeping attacks near them.

locations.village: Search plains, deserts, savannas, snowy plains and taiga for settlements on the surface.
locations.desert-pyramid: Search desert biomes for a sandstone pyramid, sometimes partly buried.
locations.jungle-temple: Look for mossy stone among dense jungle foliage; the entrance may be hidden.
locations.swamp-hut: Search swamp waterways for a small wooden hut raised on stilts.
locations.igloo: Search snowy biomes for a small snow shelter; a basement is not guaranteed.
locations.ocean-ruin: Dive through warm or cold oceans for stone or sandstone remains on the seabed.
locations.shipwreck: Scan oceans and coastlines for a wooden hull, often partly submerged.
locations.monument: Search deep oceans for a large prismarine monument below the surface.
locations.mansion: Explore dark forests or follow a woodland explorer map from a cartographer.
locations.outpost: Search open Overworld terrain for a tall pillager watchtower and surrounding cages.
locations.ruined-portal: Look for broken obsidian frames in the Overworld or Nether, often surrounded by netherrack.
locations.ancient-city: Search the deep dark far below the Overworld surface, especially beneath mountains.
locations.trail-ruins: Watch for terracotta and gravel fragments protruding from heavily forested ground.
locations.trial-chambers: Search underground across the Overworld or follow a trial explorer map from a cartographer.
locations.abandoned-camp: Search forests, taiga, savannas, swamps and other supported Overworld biomes for a campsite.
locations.fortress: Look for long Nether brick bridges and corridors crossing the Nether.
locations.bastion: Search the Nether for large, broken blackstone buildings.
locations.end-city: Travel through an End gateway to the outer islands and look for purpur towers.
locations.stronghold: Follow Eyes of Ender across the Overworld, then explore underground for stone-brick corridors.
locations.mineshaft: Search caves and underground tunnels for wooden supports, rails and minecart chests.
locations.buried-treasure: Follow a buried treasure map from a shipwreck or ocean ruin to the marked coastal area.

tips.village: Check workstations and farms first, then keep villagers safe before trading.
tips.desert-pyramid: Descend from the side and remove the stone pressure plate before entering the treasure chamber.
tips.jungle-temple: Watch for tripwires and hidden dispensers; the lever puzzle opens another compartment.
tips.swamp-hut: Fight the witch from cover or at range; a black cat may also live in the hut.
tips.igloo: Inspect the floor. Some igloos hide a basement with a villager and a zombie villager.
tips.ocean-ruin: Bring an air source and brush suspicious blocks before breaking them.
tips.shipwreck: Search the surviving compartments; a map chest can lead to buried treasure.
tips.monument: Prepare for underwater combat and Mining Fatigue from elder guardians.
tips.mansion: Clear rooms one by one and watch for evokers, which can drop totems.
tips.outpost: Approach from cover and handle crossbow pillagers before checking cages and chests.
tips.ruined-portal: Crying obsidian cannot complete a portal frame; replace it before lighting the portal.
tips.ancient-city: Carry wool to muffle vibrations while moving between the city's chests.
tips.trail-ruins: Brush suspicious gravel instead of breaking it to recover sherds and trim templates.
tips.trial-chambers: Defeat trial spawner waves for keys, then unlock vaults for their rewards.
tips.abandoned-camp: Inspect each tent and shelter; beds and cushions can provide a rest stop.
tips.fortress: Secure exposed bridges, then look for blaze spawners and nether wart.
tips.bastion: Gold armor calms ordinary piglins, but piglin brutes still attack.
tips.end-city: Bring fall protection for shulker levitation and search end ships for elytra.
tips.stronghold: Find the portal room through the corridors and watch for silverfish.
tips.mineshaft: Light the tunnels, check minecart chests and watch for cave spider spawners.
tips.buried-treasure: Use a treasure map to narrow your search, then dig near the marked spot.

onboarding.step_welcome_body: Explore your world on the map and follow discoveries into the guide.
onboarding.step_world-new_body: Add a world from here to preview its map.
onboarding.step_world-create_body: Choose the edition, version and seed, then create your map.
onboarding.step_worlds_body: Switch between linked worlds, add another save, or preview a different seed without losing your place.
onboarding.step_search_body: Search locations, enter coordinates, or jump straight to a region.
onboarding.step_filters_body: Open Menu to show or hide map layers and your saved locations.
onboarding.step_saved_body: Saved and completed locations live here, one click from the map.
onboarding.step_map-tools_body: Place personal markers anywhere, then name, colour, group and annotate them.
onboarding.step_map-dimension_body: Switch between the Overworld, Nether and End; each dimension keeps its own map view and discoveries.
onboarding.step_map-route_body: Choose a start and destination to plan a route across the current dimension.
onboarding.step_map-marker_body: Place your own marker anywhere on the map, then give it a name, group and note.
onboarding.step_map-journey_body: Show or hide the path recorded while you explore, so you can retrace where you have been.
onboarding.step_map-center_body: Jump the map back to your live in-game position whenever you lose sight of yourself.
onboarding.step_map-follow_body: Keep the map camera attached to your live position, or pause following to explore freely.
onboarding.step_map-origin_body: Return to coordinate origin and the map default view in one click; this is not your spawn point.
onboarding.step_map-zoom-out_body: Zoom out to see more of the world and understand the wider area around you.
onboarding.step_map-zoom-level_body: This number shows the current map scale, so you always know how close you are.
onboarding.step_map-zoom-in_body: Zoom in for a closer look at terrain, structures and exact positions.
onboarding.step_guide_body: Look up structures, items, mobs, enchantments and mechanics without leaving your companion app.
onboarding.step_crafting_body: Browse recipes for your edition and version, then jump into the connected guide for deeper details.
onboarding.step_account_body: Open your account to manage your profile and the features that follow you across sessions.
onboarding.step_settings-game_body: Open the desktop app, minimap or full in-game map with the game.
onboarding.step_settings-hotkeys_body: Use separate hotkeys for the desktop app, in-game map and minimap.
onboarding.step_map-controls_body: Zoom in or out to change how much of the map you see.
onboarding.step_journeys_body: Review the routes you recorded while exploring and return to places you visited.
onboarding.step_seeds_body: Compare world seeds and open a preview before creating a new world.
onboarding.step_language_body: Change the app language from the title bar at any time.
onboarding.step_settings_body: Adjust how the map and app behave, and replay this tour whenever you need it.
onboarding.step_settings-map_body: Choose how nearby markers group and how the map zooms to a selected place.
onboarding.step_settings-help_body: Use this button to replay the guided tour later.
onboarding.step_support_body: Ask for help or send feedback from inside the app.
onboarding.step_guide-item_body: Browse items and follow their details into recipes and sources.
onboarding.step_guide-entity_body: Find creatures and inspect their behavior, drops, and related entries.
onboarding.step_guide-trade_body: Browse available trades and see what each exchange offers.
onboarding.step_guide-enchantment_body: Explore enchantments and the effects they add to equipment.
onboarding.step_finish_body: Start exploring, or open Settings anytime to change options and replay this tour.
